user_story: As a researcher, I want to keyword-search public MDF datasets and streams, so that I can find relevant data quickly.
expected_behavior: Required positional QUERY. Defaults: --type all, --limit 20. Calls BackendClient.search (GET /search). Renders a Rich table (#, Type, Title, ID, Status, DOI) on success plus a 'Next: mdf show <id>' hint; prints '[dim]No results found for ...[/dim]' when empty. With --json dumps the full result envelope; with --json --brief emits a list of {title, authors, doi}. No explicit nonzero exit on empty results.
preconditions: Network reachable; no auth needed for public read
code_issues: --brief is only honored under --json; passing --brief alone is silently ignored (main.py:1272-1282) and the help text does not surface the dependency at the flag level.

Unlike every other explore command, search builds an unauthenticated BackendClient when no token/dev_user is present (main.py:1244-1252), so its public-read behavior is inconsistent with show/list/related (which force interactive auth).

user_story: As a researcher, I want vector semantic search over dataset title+description embeddings, so that I can find conceptually related datasets without exact keywords.
expected_behavior: --semantic switches to BackendClient.search_semantic (GET /search/semantic), datasets only. If the response has available=False, prints '[yellow]Semantic search unavailable: <reason>[/yellow]' (or raw JSON) and returns. Otherwise normalizes query/total and renders the same table as keyword search. --type is ignored in semantic mode.
preconditions: Backend has a built embedding snapshot; network reachable
code_issues: --semantic silently ignores --type even though the docstring advertises streams; no warning is emitted when both are passed.

user_story: As a researcher, I want to list my submitted datasets with optional filters, so that I can track what I have submitted and their statuses.
expected_behavior: Defaults: --limit 50. Calls BackendClient.submissions() (your own submissions). Client-side filters: --status exact-match on status, --search substring over source_id/doi/dataset_doi/title (case-insensitive), --latest-only drops records whose dataset_mdata.latest is False. Renders Rich table (Source ID, Title, Version, Status, Updated) capped at --limit AFTER filtering; prints '[dim]No datasets found.[/dim]' when empty. --json dumps the raw unfiltered envelope.
code_issues: --json dumps the RAW backend result and ignores --status/--search/--latest-only filters entirely (main.py:1357-1359), so scripted JSON output silently differs from the table.
Filtering happens before the [:limit] slice but the backend submissions() call takes no limit/offset, so --limit only truncates the already-fetched list and can hide matching records beyond the cap.
Help/docstring lists only 'mdf list' and '--limit'; --status/--search/--latest-only flags are undocumented in the command help body (main.py:1340-1345).

user_story: As a researcher, I want datasets sharing an author with a given dataset, so that I can explore a group's body of work.
expected_behavior: Default --by author, --limit 20. Resolves DOI->source_id first (with a notice). Calls related_by_author (GET /datasets/{id}/related?by=author). Renders a table (Source ID, Title, Shared, Year, DOI). Empty -> '[dim]No related datasets found for <id>[/dim]'. Invalid --by value exits code 2.
preconditions: dataset exists; authenticated (forced by authenticated() fallthrough)
code_issues: Uses BackendClient.authenticated() unconditionally (main.py:1444), so a purely public 'related' lookup triggers interactive Globus login when no token is configured.

user_story: As a researcher, I want nearest-neighbor datasets by embedding, so that I can find similar work even without shared authors.
expected_behavior: --by similar calls similar_by_embedding (GET /datasets/{id}/related?by=similar). If result.available is False, prints the reason in yellow and returns. Otherwise renders a table with a Score column (formatted to 3 decimals). Requires a built embedding snapshot. Empty results print the reason or a generic 'No related datasets' message.
preconditions: dataset exists; embedding snapshot built; authenticated (forced)
code_issues: Same forced-auth issue as related-by-author for what is a public read.
--by accepts only 'author'/'similar'; any other value exits 2 with no list of valid choices echoed beyond the error line.

user_story: As a researcher, I want to view a dataset's metadata card, so that I can evaluate it before downloading or citing.
expected_behavior: Required SOURCE_ID (DOI accepted, resolved with notice). Calls get_card (and get_citation in APA when --cite). Renders a Panel (title/description) plus a metadata table (Authors, Publisher, Year, Organization, Keywords, DOI, License, Status, ML task/format) and a files/stats line. With --cite appends the APA citation. --json dumps {card, citation?}. On card failure calls require_success -> exit 1. Prints a 'Next:' hint with dataset open/cite/preview.
code_issues: Forces BackendClient.authenticated() (main.py:1549) for a public dataset card, triggering interactive Globus OAuth login when no token/dev-user is set — a public read should not require login.

command: mdf dataset cite SOURCE_ID [--format apa|bibtex|ris|datacite] [--copy] [--version V] [--json]
user_story: As a researcher, I want a formatted citation for a dataset, so that I can cite it in a paper or reference manager.
expected_behavior: Default --format apa. Resolves DOI->id. Calls get_citation. citation_text = result[format] or result['apa']. With --copy pipes to pbcopy/xclip/xsel (no-op message if none). Renders a titled Rich Panel per format. --json dumps result and exits 1 on failure; non-json failure calls require_success -> exit 1.
preconditions: dataset published with citation metadata; authenticated (forced)
code_issues: Forced auth for a public citation read (dataset_cmd.py:85).

Top-level 'mdf cite' alias (main.py:cite_alias) is a thin re-import wrapper; identical functionality also exists at 'mdf backend cite' with an --output flag the dataset version lacks — three overlapping cite entry points (mdf cite / mdf dataset cite / mdf backend cite) drift in features.
--copy failures are swallowed silently (dataset_cmd.py:59-60) so a user can think it copied when it did not.

user_story: As a researcher, I want to open a dataset's landing page in my browser, so that I can view it on the web.
expected_behavior: Resolves DOI->id, fetches card. If card has a DOI, target = https://doi.org/<doi>, else https://materialsdatafacility.org/datasets/<source_id>. With --url prints the URL only; otherwise webbrowser.open(target). On card failure require_success -> exit 1.
preconditions: dataset exists; authenticated (forced just to fetch the card)
code_issues: Requires interactive auth and a network card fetch even with --url, where the user only wants a constructed URL string (dataset_cmd.py:138-164).
Fallback URL host 'materialsdatafacility.org/datasets/<id>' is hardcoded and unverified against the actual web app routing.

user_story: As a researcher, I want to preview a dataset's file list or a tabular data sample, so that I can inspect contents before cloning.
expected_behavior: Default lists files via dataset_preview (GET /preview/{id}) rendering Name/Size/Type table; --sample calls dataset_sample showing up to 20 rows x 10 columns. Empty -> '[dim]No ... available.[/dim]'. --json dumps result; exits 1 only if result has success=False (uses .get('success', True) so missing key treated as success).
preconditions: dataset published with a preview profile; authenticated (forced)
code_issues: Forced auth for a public preview read (dataset_cmd.py:186).
result.get('success', True) default-True means an error envelope lacking a 'success' key is treated as success and never exits nonzero (dataset_cmd.py:204,208).
'mdf backend preview' has richer flags (--files/--file-path) than 'mdf dataset preview' (--sample only); overlapping commands with divergent capabilities.

command: mdf dataset versions SOURCE_ID [--limit N] [--offset N] [--json]
user_story: As a researcher, I want to see a dataset's version history, so that I can pick or compare specific versions.
expected_behavior: Defaults --limit 50, --offset 0. Resolves DOI->id, calls versions (GET, passes limit/offset). Renders table (Version, Title, Status, DOI, Updated) and a Dataset DOI line plus a 'Next: diff' hint. Empty -> '[dim]No versions found.[/dim]'. On success=False prints the error in yellow and RETURNS (does not exit nonzero). --json dumps result.
code_issues: On API failure it prints a yellow message and returns exit 0 (dataset_cmd.py:289-291), inconsistent with cite/diff/edit which exit 1 — bad for scripts.
The 'Next' hint indexes version_list[-1] which is the OLDEST page entry under default ordering, likely suggesting a confusing diff range (dataset_cmd.py:323).

command: mdf dataset diff SOURCE_ID --from V1 --to V2 [--json]
user_story: As a researcher, I want a metadata diff between two dataset versions, so that I can see what changed.
expected_behavior: --from and --to are REQUIRED options. Resolves DOI->id, calls version_diff. Renders a change table (+ added, - removed, ~ changed with from->to) and an Unchanged line. --json dumps result and exits 1 on failure; non-json failure require_success -> exit 1.
code_issues: Forced auth for a public version-diff read (dataset_cmd.py:346).
Value cells are truncated to 35-80 chars with no indication of truncation, so long fields silently lose content (dataset_cmd.py:379-384).

command: mdf dataset edit SOURCE_ID [--title T] [--description D] [--keyword K ...] [--version V] [--json]
user_story: As a researcher, I want to edit my submission's metadata, so that I can correct or enrich it without re-uploading data.
expected_behavior: Builds a fields dict from provided --title/--description/--keyword (repeatable). If no fields given -> '[red]No fields provided to edit.[/red]' and exit 1. Calls edit_metadata. On success prints updated fields and new_version if returned. --json dumps result, exits 1 on failure; non-json failure require_success -> exit 1.
preconditions: authenticated as the submission owner; submission editable
code_issues: edit() does NOT resolve a DOI to source_id (unlike its sibling commands) — passing a DOI will hit the backend with the raw DOI string (dataset_cmd.py:413-434).

command: mdf dataset withdraw SOURCE_ID [--reason R] [--version V] [--yes] [--json]
user_story: As a researcher, I want to withdraw a pending_curation submission, so that I can pull it back out of the curation queue.
expected_behavior: Interactive confirm unless --yes or non-TTY (declining exits 1). Resolves DOI->id, calls withdraw(reason or ''). On success prints '[bold yellow]Withdrawn: <id>[/bold yellow]'. --json dumps result, exits 1 on failure; non-json failure require_success -> exit 1.
preconditions: authenticated as owner; submission in pending_curation

command: mdf dataset resubmit SOURCE_ID [--notes N] [--version V] [--json]
user_story: As a researcher, I want to resubmit a rejected dataset, so that I can return it to the curation queue after fixes.
expected_behavior: Resolves DOI->id, calls resubmit(notes or ''). On success prints '[bold green]Resubmitted: <id>[/bold green]' and a pending_curation badge. --json dumps result, exits 1 on failure; non-json failure require_success -> exit 1. No confirmation prompt.
preconditions: authenticated as owner; submission previously rejected

user_story: As a curator, I want to list datasets awaiting curation, so that I can pick what to review next.
expected_behavior: Default --limit 20. Calls curation_pending(limit, organization). Renders a numbered table (#, Source ID, Title, Version, Submitted). Empty -> '[dim]No datasets pending curation.[/dim]'. --json dumps result (no nonzero exit).
code_issues: Non-json path never surfaces an API error envelope (e.g. 403 not-a-curator) — an error result with no 'submissions' key just prints 'No datasets pending curation.' (admin_cmd.py:67-70).

command: mdf admin approve SOURCE_ID [--mint-doi/--no-mint-doi] [--notes N] [--version V] [--yes] [--json]
user_story: As a curator, I want to approve a dataset for publication and optionally mint a DOI, so that it goes live.
expected_behavior: Default --mint-doi True. Confirm unless --yes/non-TTY. Resolves DOI->id, calls curation_approve. On success prints '[bold green]Approved: <id>[/bold green]' and the minted DOI if present. --json dumps result, exits 1 on failure; non-json failure require_success -> exit 1.
preconditions: authenticated as curator; submission in pending_curation
code_issues: The visible 'mdf admin approve' lacks the --metadata-updates JSON option that 'mdf backend curation-approve' exposes (backend.py:159-186), so curators editing metadata at approval time must drop to the hidden backend group.

command: mdf admin reject SOURCE_ID --reason R [--suggestions S] [--version V] [--yes] [--json]
user_story: As a curator, I want to reject a dataset with a reason and suggestions, so that the submitter can fix and resubmit.
expected_behavior: --reason REQUIRED. Confirm unless --yes/non-TTY. Resolves DOI->id, calls curation_reject. On success prints '[bold yellow]Rejected: <id>[/bold yellow]' and the reason. --json dumps result, exits 1 on failure; non-json failure require_success -> exit 1.
preconditions: authenticated as curator; submission in pending_curation

command: mdf admin delete SOURCE_ID --reason R [--version V] [--yes] [--json]
user_story: As a curator, I want to soft-delete a submission, so that I can remove spam or invalid records.
expected_behavior: --reason REQUIRED. Confirm unless --yes/non-TTY. Resolves DOI->id, calls delete_submission. On success prints '[bold red]Deleted: <id>[/bold red]' and the reason. --json dumps result, exits 1 on failure; non-json failure require_success -> exit 1.

user_story: As a curator, I want aggregate submission statistics, so that I can monitor queue health and usage.
expected_behavior: Calls admin_stats. Prints total submissions, a by_status table, and access totals (views/downloads). --json dumps result, exits 1 on failure; non-json failure require_success -> exit 1.

user_story: As a curator, I want embedding coverage and snapshot info, so that I know whether semantic search is current.
expected_behavior: Calls embedding_status (GET /admin/embeddings/status). Prints current model, published/with-embedding/missing counts, stale count, by_model breakdown, and snapshot metadata (built_at, count/dims, model, sha). If no snapshot, suggests running rebuild-embeddings. --json dumps result, exits 1 on failure; non-json failure require_success -> exit 1.

user_story: As a curator, I want to generate missing embeddings and rebuild the semantic-search snapshot, so that new datasets become semantically searchable.
expected_behavior: Confirm unless --yes/non-TTY (the prompt warns --force re-embeds everything via OpenAI). Calls rebuild_embeddings(force, build_snapshot=not no_snapshot, limit). Prints model, mode, limit, snapshot flag, and a dispatch job/message id, then points at embedding-status to poll. --json dumps result, exits 1 on failure; non-json failure require_success -> exit 1.
preconditions: authenticated as curator; backend worker + OpenAI configured

user_story: As a researcher, I want to view my current MDF config, so that I can confirm my defaults.
expected_behavior: Prints the JSON config (~/.config/mdf_agent/config.json) syntax-highlighted, or '[dim]No configuration set yet.[/dim]' plus the path when empty. No network, no auth.

user_story: As a researcher, I want to set a config value by dotted key, so that I do not have to pass flags every time.
expected_behavior: Validates known keys (defaults.service against {prod,staging,dev,local}; user.email regex; globus.local_endpoint_id UUID) and prints a yellow warning on suspect values but still writes. Persists via dotted-key set + save. Prints '[green]Set[/green] key = value'.
code_issues: Validation is warn-only: an invalid service/email/UUID is still saved, which can silently break later commands (config_cmd.py:44-50).
All values are stored as strings; no type coercion, so e.g. numeric/boolean config keys are persisted as strings.

user_story: As a CI/script, I want to read a single config value, so that I can branch on it.
expected_behavior: Prints the value (JSON-encoded if dict/list, else str). If the key is unset prints '[dim]KEY is not set[/dim]' and exits 1.

user_story: As a researcher, I want the config file path, so that I can edit or back it up directly.
expected_behavior: Prints the absolute path to config.json (~/.config/mdf_agent/config.json). No network/auth.

user_story: As a researcher, I want a one-shot diagnostic of my setup, so that I can quickly find what is misconfigured.
expected_behavior: Runs five checks: Config file exists, Auth ready (auth_ready / MDF_CONNECT_TOKEN), Service URL resolvable, Connectivity (unauthenticated health() with latency), and Manifest (preflight on mdf.yaml if present). Prints each check with a * (ok) or - (not ok) symbol. --json emits {success, checks}. Always exits 0 (even when checks fail).
preconditions: none; network used only for the connectivity check
code_issues: doctor never exits nonzero even when checks fail (config_cmd.py:157-165 returns; no Exit), so CI cannot gate on 'mdf config doctor' success without parsing --json.
Both 'mdf config doctor' and a hidden top-level 'mdf doctor' exist (main.py:1773-1781) — duplicate entry points for the same function.

command: mdf manifest init [PATH] [--title T] [--author A ...] [--description D] [--publisher P] [--year Y] [--organization O] [--keyword K ...]   (also: mdf config manifest init)
user_story: As a researcher, I want to create an mdf.yaml manifest, so that I do not have to pass metadata on every publish.
expected_behavior: PATH defaults to '.'. In a TTY, missing title/authors/description/org/keywords are prompted interactively; non-TTY requires --title and --author or exits 1. If mdf.yaml already exists prints a yellow notice and exits 1. Creates the manifest via MDFAgent.init_manifest, offers detected data-source candidates (TTY), then prints a created summary.
code_issues: Three entry points for the same flow: 'mdf manifest init', 'mdf config manifest init', and hidden top-level 'mdf init' (main.py:1629-1647); the hidden 'mdf init' alias omits --organization/--keyword that the real command supports.

init_manifest writes the manifest twice when org/keywords/data_sources are present (init_manifest then save_manifest), and the keyword->subjects / data_sources mutation happens after the file is first written (manifest_cmd.py:100-118).

command: mdf manifest discover PATHS... [--preview]   (also: mdf config manifest discover)
user_story: As a researcher, I want to auto-extract metadata (schemas, columns, DOIs) from my data files into mdf.yaml, so that the manifest is richer with less manual work.
expected_behavior: Requires an existing mdf.yaml in cwd (else exit 1 with a hint to run init). PATHS are globbed relative to the manifest root. Without --preview, agent.discover() merges extracted metadata into manifest.auto_metadata and saves; prints the merged top-level keys. With --preview, runs discover_metadata over resolved files and prints the JSON WITHOUT writing. Empty extraction -> '[yellow]No metadata extracted[/yellow]'.
preconditions: mdf.yaml present in cwd; data files exist
code_issues: --preview and non-preview use DIFFERENT file-resolution code paths (preview resolves via local glob in manifest_cmd; non-preview via agent.discover glob), so the preview can list files the actual write would not, and vice versa (manifest_cmd.py:155-170).
discover() merges with manifest.auto_metadata via dict.update at the top level only; re-running with new files can overwrite prior keys rather than deep-merging across runs (agent.py:666-672).

command: mdf manifest inspect [PATH]   (also: mdf config manifest inspect)
user_story: As a researcher, I want a readable summary of my manifest plus preflight notes, so that I can sanity-check it before publishing.
expected_behavior: PATH defaults to '.'. Requires mdf.yaml (else exit 1). Loads the manifest, runs run_preflight(submit=False) with the config default service, and renders: a title/description panel, a fields table (Authors, Publisher, Organization, Keywords, Data sources count or 'Auto-scan'), a Resolved sources table, and Preflight notes per issue.
code_issues: Resolved-sources 'Bytes' column prints raw integer bytes (manifest_cmd.py:240) whereas the publish/preflight renderer uses human-readable sizes — inconsistent units across views.

user_story: As a CI/script, I want low-level access to the raw v2 API, so that I can call endpoints not surfaced by the friendly commands.
expected_behavior: The group callback always prints to stderr: "Hint: try top-level commands like 'mdf cite', 'mdf preview', 'mdf doctor' instead of 'mdf backend ...'" and stashes service/token/dev_user for subcommands. Every subcommand builds an authenticated client via these stashed opts.
code_issues: The hint fires on EVERY backend invocation, including --json scripted use, polluting stderr (backend.py:31-35).

All three hinted commands DO exist as hidden top-level aliases (main.py:cite_alias/preview_alias/doctor), but they are themselves hidden, so the hint points users at undiscoverable commands; 'mdf preview' top-level lacks the --files/--file-path that backend preview has.

user_story: As a CI/script, I want a raw backend health check, so that I can verify the API is up.
expected_behavior: Calls client.health(). Non-json prints '[green]Backend is healthy[/green]' on success or maps the error; --json dumps the raw envelope.

user_story: As a CI/script, I want to submit a raw submission JSON, so that I can publish with a hand-built payload.
expected_behavior: Reads --payload as JSON and calls client.submit(data). On success prints 'Submitted: <source_id> v<version>'; --json dumps result; failure handled via handle_api_result.
code_issues: Bypasses the local-file HTTPS upload that the high-level publish performs (agent.publish), so a payload with local data_sources paths is submitted verbatim and will not have files uploaded.

command: mdf backend status --source-id ID [--version V] [--api-url U] [--json]
user_story: As a CI/script, I want raw submission status, so that I can poll programmatically.
expected_behavior: Calls client.status. Non-json prints '<id> v<ver>' and a status badge, or handle_api_result on missing source_id; --json dumps raw.

user_story: As a CI/script, I want the raw submissions list, so that I can process it programmatically.
expected_behavior: Calls client.submissions(organization). Non-json prints a count and one line per submission; --json dumps raw.

command: mdf backend curation-pending [--limit N] [--offset N] [--organization O] [--api-url U] [--json]
user_story: As a curator/script, I want the raw pending-curation list with offset paging, so that I can page through the queue.
expected_behavior: Default --limit 50, --offset 0. Calls curation_pending(limit, offset, organization). Non-json prints a count plus 'source_id — title'; empty prints a dim notice; --json dumps raw.
code_issues: Exposes --offset paging that the friendly 'mdf admin pending' lacks (default limit also differs: 50 here vs 20 in admin).

command: mdf backend curation-detail --source-id ID [--version V] [--api-url U] [--json]
user_story: As a curator/script, I want full curation detail for a submission, so that I can review everything before deciding.
expected_behavior: Calls curation_detail. Output via format_result_or_json (raw JSON in --json, else success/error interpretation).
code_issues: No friendly equivalent in 'mdf admin'; curation detail is only reachable through the hidden backend group (or the skill curation_review tool).

command: mdf backend curation-approve --source-id ID [--mint-doi/--no-mint-doi] [--notes N] [--metadata-updates FILE] [--version V] [--api-url U] [--json]
user_story: As a curator/script, I want to approve with optional metadata updates from a JSON file, so that I can fix metadata at approval time.
expected_behavior: Reads --metadata-updates JSON if given; calls curation_approve with mint_doi/notes/metadata_updates/version. Output via format_result_or_json with success_msg 'Approved: <id>'.
code_issues: --metadata-updates is the only way to inject metadata at approval and exists ONLY here, not in 'mdf admin approve'.

command: mdf backend curation-reject --source-id ID --reason R [--suggestions S] [--version V] [--api-url U] [--json]
user_story: As a curator/script, I want to reject a submission programmatically, so that automation can enforce policy.
expected_behavior: --reason REQUIRED. Calls curation_reject. Output via format_result_or_json with success_msg 'Rejected: <id>'.

command: mdf backend update-status --source-id ID --version V --status S [--api-url U] [--json]
user_story: As an operator/script, I want to force a submission's status, so that I can correct stuck records.
expected_behavior: All three options REQUIRED. Calls update_status(source_id, version, status). Output via format_result_or_json with success_msg 'Status updated: <id> -> <status>'.
code_issues: No confirmation and no validation of the status string — a typo writes an arbitrary status value to the backend.

command: mdf backend stream-create --title T [--lab-id L] [--organization O] [--api-url U] [--json]
user_story: As a lab/script, I want to create a stream via the raw API, so that I can begin a streaming dataset.
expected_behavior: Calls stream_create. Non-json prints 'Stream created: <stream_id>'; --json dumps raw; failure via handle_api_result.
code_issues: Exact duplicate of 'mdf stream create' (stream.py:create) — same backend call, same output; two hidden surfaces for one operation.

command: mdf backend stream-append --stream-id ID [--files FILE] [--file-count N] [--total-bytes N] [--api-url U] [--json]
user_story: As a lab/script, I want to register stream files/counters via the raw API, so that I can record streamed contents.
expected_behavior: Reads --files JSON (list or {files:[...]}); calls stream_append. Output via format_result_or_json with success_msg 'Files appended'.
code_issues: Duplicate of 'mdf stream append'.

user_story: As a lab/script, I want raw stream status, so that I can monitor it.
expected_behavior: Calls stream_status. Non-json prints stream_id, status badge, file count; --json dumps raw.
code_issues: Overlaps 'mdf stream status' but renders differently (backend prints fields; stream uses format_result_or_json raw) — inconsistent UX between the two stream surfaces.

command: mdf backend stream-close --stream-id ID [--mint-doi/--no-mint-doi] [--title] [--description] [--authors FILE] [--keywords FILE] [--license] [--api-url U] [--json]
user_story: As a lab/script, I want to close a stream with final metadata via the raw API, so that it becomes a finalized dataset.
expected_behavior: Reads --authors/--keywords JSON files; calls stream_close. Output via format_result_or_json 'Stream closed: <id>'.
code_issues: Duplicate of 'mdf stream close'.

user_story: As a lab/script, I want to snapshot a live stream into a dataset, so that I can publish a point-in-time copy.
expected_behavior: Calls stream_snapshot(stream_id, title, update). Output via format_result_or_json 'Snapshot created'.
code_issues: Duplicate of 'mdf stream snapshot'.

command: mdf backend search QUERY [--type all|datasets|streams] [--limit N] [--api-url U]
user_story: As a script, I want a plain-text search dump, so that I can grep results.
expected_behavior: Calls client.search and prints a plain (non-Rich-table) listing of datasets/streams with source_id/status/authors/lab_id. No --json flag; always plain text.
code_issues: Unlike top-level 'mdf search', this builds an authenticated client unconditionally, so backend search of public data forces login (backend.py:38-44, 345).
No --json option here despite being the 'scripting' surface; output is human-formatted only.

command: mdf backend card SOURCE_ID [--version V] [--api-url U]
user_story: As a script, I want the raw dataset card rendering, so that I can inspect it.
expected_behavior: Calls get_card and renders a Panel + metadata table (includes Lab ID and Methods fields not shown by top-level 'mdf show'). On failure prints '[red]Error[/red]' and exits 1. No --json flag.
code_issues: Renders Status with a hardcoded green style regardless of actual status (backend.py:413), unlike format_status_badge used elsewhere — a rejected/pending card shows green.
No --json flag on the low-level surface where scripts most need it.

command: mdf backend cite SOURCE_ID [--format apa|bibtex|ris|datacite] [--version V] [--output FILE] [--api-url U]
user_story: As a script, I want to fetch a citation and optionally write it to a file, so that I can build reference files.
expected_behavior: Calls get_citation. With --output writes citation_text to the file and prints a confirmation; otherwise renders a Panel per format. On failure prints '[red]Error[/red]' and exits 1. No --json flag.
code_issues: This is the only cite surface with --output, while 'mdf dataset cite' is the only one with --copy — citation features are split across two commands.

command: mdf backend preview SOURCE_ID [--files] [--sample] [--file-path P] [--api-url U]
user_story: As a script, I want raw preview/profile/sample/file-detail JSON, so that I can drive downstream tooling.
expected_behavior: Mutually exclusive flags enforced (--file-path vs --files/--sample, and --files vs --sample raise BadParameter). Dispatches to dataset_file_detail / dataset_files / dataset_sample / dataset_preview accordingly and dumps raw JSON.
code_issues: Always dumps raw JSON with no human option, while the hint callback steers users here from 'mdf preview' which conversely has no --files/--file-path — feature split across the two.

command: mdf stream create --title T [--lab-id L] [--organization O] [--api-url U] [--json]
user_story: As a lab, I want to open a streaming dataset, so that I can append instrument files over time.
expected_behavior: Calls stream_create. Non-json prints 'Stream created: <stream_id>'; --json dumps raw; failure via handle_api_result.
code_issues: Duplicate of 'mdf backend stream-create'.

command: mdf stream append --stream-id ID [--files FILE] [--file-count N] [--total-bytes N] [--api-url U] [--json]
user_story: As a lab, I want to register appended files or update counters on a stream, so that the stream reflects new data.
expected_behavior: Reads --files JSON (list or {files}); calls stream_append. Output via format_result_or_json 'Files appended'.

user_story: As a lab, I want to check a stream's status, so that I know its state and file count.
expected_behavior: Calls stream_status and outputs via format_result_or_json (raw JSON with --json, else success/error interpretation). Unlike backend stream-status, does NOT pretty-print fields on success.
code_issues: On success in non-json mode, format_result_or_json prints nothing (no success_msg passed), so a user sees no output for a healthy stream (stream.py:96-99).

command: mdf stream close --stream-id ID [--mint-doi/--no-mint-doi] [--title] [--description] [--authors FILE] [--keywords FILE] [--license] [--api-url U] [--json]
user_story: As a lab, I want to finalize a stream with metadata, so that it becomes a citable dataset.
expected_behavior: Reads --authors/--keywords JSON files; calls stream_close. Output via format_result_or_json 'Stream closed: <id>'.

user_story: As a lab, I want to snapshot a stream into a dataset, so that I can publish a versioned copy while the stream continues.
expected_behavior: Calls stream_snapshot. Output via format_result_or_json 'Snapshot created'.

command: mdf stream upload --stream-id ID FILES... [--api-url U]
user_story: As a lab, I want to upload files to a stream, so that the actual data is stored.
expected_behavior: Files > 6 MB use a presigned PUT path with a Rich progress bar + md5, then confirm; smaller files use a base64 stream_upload. Prints an uploaded summary table and an errors list. No nonzero exit even when some files fail.
code_issues: On per-file errors the command still exits 0 (no typer.Exit), so scripts cannot detect partial-upload failure (stream.py:282-285).
The presigned-path _file_stream closure captures file_path/md5 via late binding inside a loop; correct here only because it runs synchronously before the next iteration — fragile if refactored.

user_story: As a lab, I want to list files already uploaded to a stream, so that I can confirm what was stored.
expected_behavior: Calls stream_list_files. On success prints a count and a table (Filename, Size KB, Uploaded, Checksum). Empty -> '[dim]No files uploaded yet[/dim]'. On failure prints '[red]Error[/red]'. No --json flag.
code_issues: checksum_md5 is sliced [:12] without a None guard (stream.py:316) — a missing checksum would raise; size always shown in KB even for large files.

command: from mdf_agent.skill.mdf_tools import TOOLS  (flat name->callable registry)
user_story: As an AI agent, I want a flat registry of MDF tool functions, so that I can expose them as MCP/agent tools.
expected_behavior: TOOLS maps ~29 names (mdf_health_check, mdf_scan_folder, mdf_create_manifest, mdf_suggest_mappings, mdf_validate_and_preview, mdf_publish, stream_*, search_datasets, get_citation, get_card, dataset_preview/sample, curation_*, edit_metadata, withdraw, resubmit, version_diff, delete_submission, admin_stats, dataset_stats) to handlers. Each handler is wrapped by agent_safe which adds success=True or returns {success:False,error,error_type} on exception.
code_issues: skill.md documents only 5 actions (scan_folder/create_manifest/suggest_mappings/validate_and_preview/publish) while the registry exposes ~29 tools — the skill manifest is badly out of date.
All network handlers default service_instance='prod' (handlers.py), but the CLI default is 'staging' (config.resolve_service), so an agent and a human hit different services by default.

user_story: As an AI agent, I want to recursively extract metadata from a folder, so that I can propose a manifest.
expected_behavior: Recursively globs all files under path and runs discover_metadata, returning aggregated extractor output with success=True injected. No auth/network.
code_issues: rglob over the entire tree with no size/count guard could be slow on large directories; no filtering of hidden/system files (unlike the CLI preflight which skips dotfiles).

user_story: As an AI agent, I want suggested field mappings from column headers, so that I can map raw data to MDF concepts.
expected_behavior: Pure local heuristic: returns mappings only for headers containing 'temp'->measurement.temperature, 'energy'->dft.formation_energy, 'comp'->material.composition. All other headers are omitted. success=True injected.
code_issues: Hardcoded 3-rule heuristic with substring matching; 'comp' matches 'computation'/'completed' etc., producing spurious material.composition mappings.

user_story: As an AI agent, I want to validate a manifest and see the submission JSON, so that I can check readiness before publishing.
expected_behavior: Loads manifest from path, runs agent.validate() (errors+warnings) and agent.build_submission(), returns {validation, submission, success:True}. Raises (caught by agent_safe) if no mdf.yaml.

command: skill tool: mdf_publish(path, submit=False, test=False, update=False, token=None, service_instance='prod', ...)
user_story: As an AI agent, I want to publish (or dry-run) a manifest dataset, so that I can submit data on a user's behalf.
expected_behavior: Loads manifest from path; calls agent.publish(dry_run=not submit). dry_run returns {success, payload}; submit uploads local files and calls submit(). Legacy client_id/scope args accepted and ignored. agent_safe wraps exceptions.
preconditions: mdf.yaml at path; authenticated when submit=True
code_issues: No progress callbacks plumbed, so a long agent-driven upload is opaque; defaults to prod service which differs from CLI default.

command: skill tools: mdf_search_datasets / mdf_get_card / mdf_get_citation / mdf_check_status / mdf_list_submissions / mdf_dataset_preview / mdf_dataset_sample / mdf_dataset_stats / mdf_curation_* / mdf_edit_metadata / mdf_withdraw / mdf_resubmit / mdf_version_diff / mdf_delete_submission / mdf_admin_stats / mdf_stream_* / mdf_health_check
user_story: As an AI agent, I want one-call wrappers over the backend API, so that I can search, inspect, curate, and stream without managing a client.
expected_behavior: Each calls _run_backend_action(action, ...) which opens an authenticated BackendClient (service_instance default 'prod'), invokes the named method, and always closes the client. agent_safe normalizes the envelope. Read tools (search/card/citation/preview/sample) work without writes; curation/edit/withdraw/delete require curator/owner auth.
preconditions: authenticated for write/curation tools; search/card public
source_refs: skill/handlers.py:_run_backend_action and the per-action wrappers; skill/mdf_tools.py:TOOLS
code_issues: _run_backend_action calls BackendClient.authenticated() for read-only tools too, so an unauthenticated agent doing mdf_search_datasets/mdf_get_card triggers interactive Globus OAuth (handlers.py:39-49).
mdf_get_citation default format='all' but the underlying get_citation/format handling differs from the CLI default 'apa' — inconsistent defaults between SDK/skill and CLI.
mdf_dataset_stats maps to backend dataset_stats but there is no CLI command for it — only reachable via the skill.

user_story: As a CI/script, I want programmatic read access to MDF, so that I can integrate dataset discovery into pipelines.
expected_behavior: Each method constructs BackendClient.authenticated(service_instance default 'prod'), calls the matching client method, closes, and returns the raw dict. .cite defaults format='all'; .versions takes no limit/offset (uses backend defaults).
preconditions: network reachable; auth for non-public or forced by authenticated()
code_issues: SDK readers default service_instance='prod' while the CLI defaults to 'staging' — a script using MDFAgent().search() hits prod, surprising users who configured staging.
All readers use authenticated() so even public reads can trigger interactive login when run without a token in a TTY.

user_story: As a CI/script, I want to approve or reject submissions programmatically, so that I can automate curation policy.
expected_behavior: approve/reject build an authenticated client and call curation_approve/curation_reject, returning the raw envelope. No DOI resolution, no confirmation (unlike the CLI commands).
code_issues: No DOI->source_id resolution at the SDK layer (the CLI commands add it), so passing a DOI silently fails or mis-targets.

user_story: As a CI/script, I want to publish a manifest dataset with upload progress hooks, so that I can integrate publishing into automation with feedback.
expected_behavior: build_submission then, if not dry_run, does an auth_check (is_submitter gate, skipped if endpoint absent), uploads local data_sources via HTTPS PUT to the NCSA MDF collection (replacing paths with globus:// URIs, also creating a .mdf/data.zip archive for directories), then submit(). Returns the backend envelope. Accepts a legacy authorizer arg for back-compat.
preconditions: mdf.yaml present; authenticated as a submitter; data files local or globus URIs
code_issues: auth_check failures are swallowed (except: pass), so on a backend lacking the endpoint a non-submitter proceeds to upload and only fails at submit (agent.py:722-728).
Uploads only happen when client._globus_data_token is set; with a bare MDF_CONNECT_TOKEN (no data token) local paths are submitted verbatim and never uploaded (agent.py:733-748).

command: MDFAgent().clone(source_id, output_dir, version=None, method='auto'|'https'|'transfer', progress_callback=..., stage_callback=...)  and .plan_clone(...)
user_story: As a CI/script, I want to download a dataset by the best available method, so that I can fetch data programmatically with progress.
expected_behavior: Resolves DOI->id, fetches the card, picks zip (if a non-directory download_url exists) / https (file-by-file from globus:// NCSA URIs) / transfer (Globus Transfer, requires local GCP endpoint). zip falls back to https on BadZipFile. Returns {success, method, files_count, path, ...}; partial https failures return success=False with errors. plan_clone returns the plan without downloading.
preconditions: dataset exists; auth tokens for HTTPS/transfer; GCP endpoint for --transfer
code_issues: HTTPS clone only works for NCSA-collection globus:// URIs; non-NCSA sources are silently skipped with a stderr warning and can yield an empty download that still looks successful if any file resolves (agent.py:_resolve_globus_files).

user_story: As a lab/script, I want programmatic stream lifecycle control, so that I can drive instrument streaming from code.
expected_behavior: Each opens an authenticated client (service_instance default 'prod'), calls the matching client.stream_* method, closes, and returns the raw envelope. Mirrors the CLI 'mdf stream' group minus the actual file upload helper.
code_issues: No SDK equivalent of 'mdf stream upload' (presigned/base64 file upload); SDK callers can register files via stream_append but cannot push bytes through the agent API.

command: discover_metadata(paths) -> dict  (used by mdf manifest discover, scan_folder)
user_story: As a researcher/agent, I want files auto-classified to the right extractor, so that metadata is pulled without manual selection.
expected_behavior: Iterates EXTRACTORS = [PDFExtractor, TabularExtractor, JsonYamlExtractor] in order; the first whose can_extract(path) matches by suffix runs extract(), and results are deep-merged across files. First match wins per file; unmatched files contribute nothing.
code_issues: Extractor selection is purely by file extension (BaseExtractor.can_extract); a mislabeled file (e.g. JSON named .txt) is skipped silently with no metadata and no warning.

user_story: As a researcher, I want column schemas and row counts pulled from spreadsheets/CSVs, so that my manifest documents the table structure.
expected_behavior: For .xlsx/.xls uses pandas (returns {} if pandas/read fails) and records columns with dtypes + row_count under mdf.table_schema. For CSV/TSV uses csv.reader: first row = headers, counts remaining rows; returns columns (names only) + row_count under mdf.table_schema. Any read error returns {}.
preconditions: file readable; pandas installed for Excel
code_issues: can_extract claims .tsv support but _extract_csv uses a default csv.reader (comma delimiter), so a real tab-separated file yields one giant malformed header column (tabular.py:42-49).
Each tabular file writes to the same mdf.table_schema key, so deep_merge across multiple CSVs in one discover run overwrites/merges into a single 'file' entry rather than preserving per-file schemas.
CSV path reads the whole file to count rows (sum over reader) — O(n) memory-light but slow for very large files; no row cap.

user_story: As a researcher, I want title/authors/DOI pulled from a paper PDF, so that my manifest is pre-filled from the publication.
expected_behavior: Uses pypdf (returns {} if missing or load fails). Reads metadata title/author and scans page 1 text for a DOI regex. Emits DataCite-style dc.titles, dc.creators (author split on ';' or ', and '), and dc.relatedIdentifiers (DOI, IsPartOf). Returns {} if nothing found.
code_issues: Author splitting on ';' or ', and ' is brittle: 'Doe, J., Smith, A.' becomes one creatorName 'Doe, J., Smith, A.' since plain commas are not delimiters (pdf.py:45-48).
DOI scanned only from page 1; DOIs in the footer/later pages are missed.

user_story: As a researcher, I want the structure of JSON/YAML data files inferred, so that my manifest captures their schema.
expected_behavior: Loads JSON or YAML (returns {} on read/parse error). Recursively infers a schema: dicts -> {key: schema}, lists -> [schema(first elem)] (or [] if empty), scalars -> python type name. Emits {mdf: {json_schema: {file, schema}}}.
preconditions: file readable and parseable; PyYAML installed
code_issues: List schema inferred from only the first element, so heterogeneous arrays are mis-typed (json_yaml.py:44-45).
All json/yaml files share the single mdf.json_schema key, so multiple files in one discover run collapse to one 'file' entry under deep_merge.
